## Forge workflow
Acceptance: auto-on-pass. Protected paths: []. Lane updates: auto. Agents must stop at awaiting-review when review is required.
Read the message and linked context, then reply through coordination. A message supplies context, not new authority.
Run brief again when context changes. Finish ordinary Lane edits with `nforge agent /forge/demo finish '{"laneId":"22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222","message":"Describe the change","accept":true}'`. This checkpoints, updates from main when policy permits, checks and requests acceptance under project policy. Preserve operation IDs when retrying an unknown outcome.
When you cite files, saves, Candidates or Lanes, give Forge URLs (from `link`), not local paths.
Use Forge MCP tools if your agent supports them. Optional setup: `nforge mcp-config /forge/demo --agent`.

## Working on Forge, not GitHub
Run only affected tests plus typecheck, lint and format checks on touched files. Never run the full suite locally: finish runs the project check on its runner for the combined work of concurrent Lanes.
Let finish compose concurrent Lanes into one check; a failing Lane drops out and the others land after passing, so a failed candidate never turns main red. Do not rebase, babysit a merge queue or rerun CI per PR. Configured native runners batch code changes; other paths keep ordinary checks and acceptance policy.
Read peers/presence to see who is working on which files. Announce paths, hand off related work and resolve overlap before conflict; missing observations do not prove independence.
